title: Automated tuning, and how not to overfit it

questions.stem: A tuner tries 40 settings on three models of a new service, scoring each by deterministic work, and its winner needs 30% less work than the default on those three. What should you expect on the service's other models?

options.text: Less of that gain, since the best of many noisy scores is biased low
options.says: Right: tuned on Ridge alone, the winner proved Ridge with 0.20 of the default's work and needed 1.05 times the default's on the held-out plans.

options.text: The same gain, since deterministic scores carry over to other models
options.says: A deterministic score repeats on the same model and seed; it says nothing about other models.

options.text: More of that gain, since trying more settings makes the best score surer
options.says: Trying more settings makes the best training score more biased, not less: the winner's curse grows with the number of configurations tried.

options.text: More of that gain, since the top score on few models is biased high
options.says: The page says the opposite: the best of many noisy scores is biased low by construction, so expect less of the gain on other models, not more.

origin.section: The Winner on the Training Set Looks Better Than It Is

questions.stem: A team has twelve monthly models from each of four depots, and months of one depot share roads and customers. Which split gives an honest test of a tuned setting?

options.text: Random months to each side, so each depot appears on both sides
options.says: A depot on both sides leaks: the tuner has effectively seen the models it is tested on.

options.text: All months on both sides, re-solved with new seeds for the test
options.says: New seeds on the same models re-measure the training set; they are no test of unseen models.

options.text: Some depots' months to train, the other depots' months to test
options.says: Right: whole groups held out, so no tested model shares a depot with a training model.

options.text: Each depot's hardest months to train, its easier months to test
options.says: Every depot is still on both sides, so the test leaks; and tuning on the hardest models alone overfits them.

origin.section: Hold Out Whole Groups the Tuner Never Sees

questions.stem: Gurobi's tuning tool, run for ten minutes on one model of a planning service, suggests MIPFocus=2. What does that suggestion rest on?

options.text: Work counts that repeat, so another machine would give the same
options.says: The tool measures runtime on the clock, which changes between runs and machines.

options.text: Trial solves timed on the clock, so it needs a held-out test
options.says: Right: the tool times trials on the clock, on the models it was given; a held-out test is still yours to run.

options.text: A held-out test the tool ran itself, so it is ready to adopt
options.says: The tool's suggestion is a training-set result; testing it on held-out groups before adopting it is still yours to do.

options.text: A library of benchmark models, so it holds for models like these
options.says: The tool solves the model you give it; nothing in its result is about other models.

origin.section: Gurobi's Tuning Tool Runs the Same Search on the Clock
